questions.prompt: A track is at x = 100 px with velocity +5 px/frame. Under constant velocity, what is the predicted x one frame later? (integer)
Position noise has sigma = 2 px. Using the 95% chi-square value 5.991 for 2 degrees of freedom, what is the circular gate radius in pixels? (precision 0.05)
Why can a nearest-neighbour tracker that matches detections to the LAST positions swap identities when two objects cross?
options: After they move, the detection nearest A's old position can be B's new position
The detector outputs the wrong class for one of the two crossing objects
Detections arrive unordered, so the matcher cannot keep the track order stable
The gate is always too large, so every detection is accepted by every track
questions.explanation: Predicting forward before matching removes most such swaps.

questions.prompt: Cost matrix [[1, 2], [2, 10]] with gate 20. What is the total cost of the greedy (smallest-first) assignment? (integer)
A sequence has 500 ground-truth instances, 30 misses, 10 false positives and 10 identity switches. Compute MOTA (precision 0.001).
A tracker deletes a track after its first missed detection. What happens when an object is occluded for two frames?
options: The tracker crashes because no detection is matched
The object reappears with a new ID (fragmentation)
Nothing happens, the identity is kept through the gap
The velocity estimate doubles over the missing frames
questions.explanation: Allow several misses while predicting, then delete.

questions.prompt: A robot follows one person in a corridor with others. Describe how you keep the right identity through a short occlusion and what the robot does if the identity is lost.
rubric: Keeps predicting the lost track for a few frames and gates the reappearing detection.
Uses appearance and not only distance for association.
Defines a safe behaviour when the target is lost (stop or search) rather than switching to the nearest person.
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.
